turns.question: Average review score for late deliveries vs on-time deliveries

FROM order_facts

GROUP BY delivery_status
ORDER BY delivery_status

WITH delivered_orders AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT order_id, customer_state
    FROM order_facts
    WHERE is_delivered = true
),
category_revenue AS (
    SELECT 
        s.category,
        d.customer_state,
        SUM(s.revenue) AS revenue
    FROM sales s
    JOIN delivered_orders d ON s.order_id = d.order_id
    WHERE s.purchase_year = 2017
    GROUP BY s.category, d.customer_state
)
SELECT 
    category,
    customer_state,
    ROUND(revenue, 2) AS revenue
FROM category_revenue

turns.ask: How does that compare with 2018?
turns.question: Compare the top 5 product categories by revenue in 2017, broken down by customer state, only counting orders that were actually delivered, with the same metrics in 2018 compared side by side.
turns.sql:
WITH top_categories AS (
    SELECT category
    FROM sales
    WHERE purchase_year = 2017
      AND is_delivered
    GROUP BY category
    ORDER BY SUM(revenue) DESC
    LIMIT 5
),
combined AS (
    SELECT 
        s.category,
        f.customer_state,
        s.purchase_year,
        SUM(s.revenue) AS revenue,
        COUNT(DISTINCT s.order_id) AS orders
    FROM sales s
    JOIN order_facts f ON f.order_id = s.order_id
    JOIN top_categories tc ON tc.category = s.category
    WHERE s.is_delivered
      AND f.is_delivered
      AND f.is_sale
    GROUP BY s.category, f.customer_state, s.purchase_year
)
SELECT 
    category,
    customer_state,
    ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN purchase_year = 2017 THEN revenue ELSE 0 END), 2) AS revenue_2017,
    COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN purchase_year = 2017 THEN orders END) AS orders_2017,
    ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN purchase_year = 2018 THEN revenue ELSE 0 END), 2) AS revenue_2018,
    COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN purchase_year = 2018 THEN orders END) AS orders_2018
FROM combined
GROUP BY category, customer_state
ORDER BY category, revenue_2017 DESC

results.question: Compare the top 5 product categories by revenue in 2017, broken down by customer state, only counting orders that were actually delivered, with the same metrics in 2018 compared side by side.
results.sql:
WITH top_categories AS (
    SELECT category
    FROM sales
    WHERE purchase_year = 2017
      AND is_delivered
    GROUP BY category
    ORDER BY SUM(revenue) DESC
    LIMIT 5
),
combined AS (
    SELECT 
        s.category,
        f.customer_state,
        s.purchase_year,
        SUM(s.revenue) AS revenue,
        COUNT(DISTINCT s.order_id) AS orders
    FROM sales s
    JOIN order_facts f ON f.order_id = s.order_id
    JOIN top_categories tc ON tc.category = s.category
    WHERE s.is_delivered
      AND f.is_delivered
      AND f.is_sale
    GROUP BY s.category, f.customer_state, s.purchase_year
)
SELECT 
    category,
    customer_state,
    ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN purchase_year = 2017 THEN revenue ELSE 0 END), 2) AS revenue_2017,
    COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN purchase_year = 2017 THEN orders END) AS orders_2017,
    ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN purchase_year = 2018 THEN revenue ELSE 0 END), 2) AS revenue_2018,
    COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN purchase_year = 2018 THEN orders END) AS orders_2018
FROM combined
GROUP BY category, customer_state
ORDER BY category, revenue_2017 DESC
